director.chapterArc: Measured hyperfocus holds the opening terror at a distance; Marta’s death breaks that control, then the stranger’s arrival turns chaos into disorienting tactical awe. The action contracts around impossible choices—Garrick holding the bend, the stranger spending both hands, Toren accepting two attackers—before Garrick disappears from view. Violence then drains into uncanny dust, borrowed life, and the final revelation that no rescuers remain, leaving Toren in numb paralysis.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder grounded and observational. Fear lives in delayed hearing, failed movement, shaking limbs, and precise arithmetic; awe is baffled recalculation, never superhero spectacle. Garrick and the stranger retain flat authority. Marta’s and Garrick’s losses land through facts and unfinished duties, with no elegiac swell. Return fully to base after every colored passage.

cues.delivery: Make the repeated duration a coping mechanism: exact, detached, and quietly trapped inside the memory; never rush the count or advertise panic.
cues.from: His father held the bend for two minutes.
cues.through: Two minutes is a long time.
cues.reason: The chapter establishes Toren’s dissociated hyperfocus and its lifelong persistence.

cues.delivery: A single clean command bark with absolute paternal authority; urgency is carried by precision, not vocal chaos.
cues.from: "Wheel!" his father shouted, without turning. "Wheel!"
cues.through: "Wheel!" his father shouted, without turning. "Wheel!"
cues.reason: The text explicitly marks Garrick’s shouted command, and it must override hesitation.

cues.delivery: Keep the injury and Wyck’s blows brutally factual; let the horror emerge from Senna’s raised arm and the unnecessary final strikes, not from melodrama.
cues.from: Senna did not scream. She got her arm up. She was seventy-three years old and there was almost nothing left of her and she got her arm up between it and her throat, and it opened her forearm and her shoulder, and then Wyck hit it off her with a length of rebar he had been carrying since Sallow Creek for exactly no reason at all, and it went over the side, and Wyck hit it again on the ground, and then twice more after it had stopped moving.
cues.through: Senna did not scream. She got her arm up. She was seventy-three years old and there was almost nothing left of her and she got her arm up between it and her throat, and it opened her forearm and her shoulder, and then Wyck hit it off her with a length of rebar he had been carrying since Sallow Creek for exactly no reason at all, and it went over the side, and Wyck hit it again on the ground, and then twice more after it had stopped moving.
cues.reason: The attack converts general danger into intimate bodily harm.

cues.delivery: Marta protects Milo by making her voice surgical and usable; warmth stays buried beneath exact instructions.
cues.from: "That's all I have," she said. "Milo. Milo, look at me. Press here. Both hands, all your weight, and don't lift them to look."
cues.through: "That's all I have," she said. "Milo. Milo, look at me. Press here. Both hands, all your weight, and don't lift them to look."
cues.reason: Her maternal care appears as disciplined crisis control.

cues.delivery: A small, involuntary fracture from Milo—unfinished, disbelieving, and immediately contained.
cues.from: "Mum —"
cues.through: "Mum —"
cues.reason: The single word exposes the child’s dependence before Marta restores the task.

cues.delivery: Fracture the reasoning without speeding it up: Toren keeps rerunning the distance and finds no possible rescue.
cues.from: Toren saw it happen, and it was three steps away, and he could not get there. There was no version of it, run any way he tried to run it, where he got there.
cues.through: Toren saw it happen, and it was three steps away, and he could not get there. There was no version of it, run any way he tried to run it, where he got there.
cues.reason: This is the helpless realization immediately before Marta’s death.

cues.delivery: State Marta’s fall plainly, then give Milo’s unnameable sound weight without imitating it; the cruel center is that his hands remain obedient.
cues.from: Marta Faust went down under it, and the wall went out like a lamp, and Milo made a sound that Toren had no name for and did not let go of his grandmother's shoulder, because his mother had told him not to.
cues.through: Marta Faust went down under it, and the wall went out like a lamp, and Milo made a sound that Toren had no name for and did not let go of his grandmother's shoulder, because his mother had told him not to.
cues.reason: Death and duty collide in the chapter’s first irreversible loss.

cues.delivery: Land the impossibility with baffled certainty, not wonder: Toren has observed a fact that should not exist.
cues.from: He did not fall. That was the first wrong thing.
cues.through: He did not fall. That was the first wrong thing.
cues.reason: The stranger’s descent introduces the first violation of Toren’s physical rules.

cues.delivery: Let Toren’s known world quietly collapse. Preserve the careful explanation of the one-at-a-time rule, then make its violation feel mechanically impossible rather than magnificent.
cues.from: Toren stood there with a crooked grey spike sticking out of his own fist, and the whole bottom fell out of his understanding of the world.
cues.through: The man on the road was doing both, at the same time, and he was doing them the way a person breathes with both lungs.
cues.reason: Toren recognizes that the stranger is sustaining two Ember functions simultaneously.

cues.delivery: A sharp relay of understood orders; Toren borrows the stranger’s authority because hesitation will kill them.
cues.from: "Dessa!" he shouted. "North — get him moving north, go!"
cues.through: "Dessa!" he shouted. "North — get him moving north, go!"
cues.reason: The text explicitly marks Toren’s shouted command at the escape reversal.

cues.delivery: Give the bare sentence full finality without swelling it; this is recognition arriving before Toren can process it.
cues.from: Garrick did not go with them.
cues.through: Garrick did not go with them.
cues.reason: Garrick’s decision to remain behind becomes irrevocable.

cues.delivery: A strained worker’s mantra forced through failing control, addressed to his own arm rather than to the others.
cues.from: "Hold —" the man on the road said, to no one, to himself, to his own shaking arm. "Hold, hold —"
cues.through: "Hold —" the man on the road said, to no one, to himself, to his own shaking arm. "Hold, hold —"
cues.reason: The stranger’s composure briefly reveals the physical cost of holding the pinch.

cues.delivery: Keep the inventory flat and exact; allow desperation only as pressure beneath the ledger of two hands already spent.
cues.from: "If I let go of this, everything behind it comes through in one go, and the cart is still on the wrong side of me." He did not turn his head. His left arm was shaking properly now, all the way to the shoulder. "I have a blade and I have this and I have two hands, and I have already spent them both. So it's yours. Two of them. On this side. Say yes."
cues.through: "If I let go of this, everything behind it comes through in one go, and the cart is still on the wrong side of me." He did not turn his head. His left arm was shaking properly now, all the way to the shoulder. "I have a blade and I have this and I have two hands, and I have already spent them both. So it's yours. Two of them. On this side. Say yes."
cues.reason: The stranger transfers an impossible responsibility to Toren while concealing his own alarm.

cues.delivery: Deliver the ultimatum without threat-display: a calm statement of consequences from someone who truly will release the barrier.
cues.from: "Say yes, or say no and I'll drop it now and we'll all find out together."
cues.through: "Say yes, or say no and I'll drop it now and we'll all find out together."
cues.reason: Toren must accept responsibility immediately or face collective death.

cues.delivery: Hold Toren’s retrospective longing under strict control. Count the axe strokes clearly; let the bend, not the voice, cut his father away.
cues.from: He did not look back. Toren wanted that later and never got it. Garrick Voss stood facing the wrong way with his shoulders set and swung the axe at the knee, and again, and again, and the fourth time he was slow, and after that the bend came between them, and Toren could not see him.
cues.through: He did not look back. Toren wanted that later and never got it. Garrick Voss stood facing the wrong way with his shoulders set and swung the axe at the knee, and again, and again, and the fourth time he was slow, and after that the bend came between them, and Toren could not see him.
cues.reason: This is Toren’s final sight of Garrick and the chapter’s central emotional severance.

cues.delivery: Shift into eerie observation. Describe the dissolution slowly enough to follow its physics, with revulsion contained inside Toren’s humming teeth.
cues.from: The bodies went to dust.
cues.through: Toren had heard about that. Everybody had heard about that — it was the one thing every story about Riftspawn agreed on, that they did not leave bodies. Seeing it was different: the husks sagged where they lay and lost their edges and came apart into a fine drifting grey that did not blow away, that pooled and ran down the camber of the road like water finding a low place. Where enough of it collected, it thickened into something with a shine on it, a slow slick of it in the seams of the old road bed, and it made Toren's back teeth hum the same way the wall had.
cues.reason: The violence ends and the husks become an uncanny material phenomenon.

cues.delivery: Keep Wyck absolutely level and depleted; each repetition narrows the surviving world without any overt lament.
cues.from: "That was them," Wyck said. He was leaning on the cart with the rebar still in his fist, and his knuckles were split, and he sounded absolutely level, which was worse than shouting. "That's all of them. That's all there was."
cues.through: "That was them," Wyck said. He was leaning on the cart with the rebar still in his fist, and his knuckles were split, and he sounded absolutely level, which was worse than shouting. "That's all of them. That's all there was."
cues.reason: The stranger learns that the dead were the group’s entire adult support.

cues.delivery: Quiet, inward refusal from a man recognizing a new obligation; preserve the house-and-door image as dread, not theatrical mystery.
cues.from: "No," he said.
cues.through: He said it quietly, and not to any of them. He said it the way a man says it to a door he has just heard open somewhere behind him in a house he was sure was empty.
cues.reason: The stranger’s professional reserve finally cracks in private.

cues.delivery: Treat the covering of bodies as practical respect. No elegy—only hands restoring order where life cannot be restored.
cues.from: Then he turned around and walked south down the cut, past them, past the wheel ruts, to where Marta Faust was, and Toren watched him crouch down and straighten her arms and put her coat over her face, and go on to the next one, and do the same.
cues.through: Then he turned around and walked south down the cut, past them, past the wheel ruts, to where Marta Faust was, and Toren watched him crouch down and straighten her arms and put her coat over her face, and go on to the next one, and do the same.
cues.reason: The stranger answers the revelation through burial-like duty.

cues.delivery: Slow into physical paralysis while keeping the inventory lucid; land the final inability as numb fact, not a cry.
cues.from: Toren stood in the middle of the road with his father's Ember gone cold and slack in his fist and the disk hanging under his shirt where nobody could see it — and did not go with the man, and did not go around the bend, and could not make his legs do either thing.
cues.through: Toren stood in the middle of the road with his father's Ember gone cold and slack in his fist and the disk hanging under his shirt where nobody could see it — and did not go with the man, and did not go around the bend, and could not make his legs do either thing.
cues.reason: Toren ends unable to choose between following the living and finding his father.

pauses.after: quiet at the top of it.

pauses.reason: Prepare the reversal hidden inside Garrick’s protective order.

pauses.before: the noise from the north changed
pauses.reason: Signal the arrival of a new force before its source is visible.
Give Toren’s collapse of understanding a distinct landing.
Prepare the precise impossibility at the center of the stranger’s ability.

pauses.before: I have already spent them both.
pauses.reason: Land the stranger’s two-hand arithmetic before responsibility passes to Toren.
Prepare the credible consequence beneath the flat ultimatum.

pauses.before: the fourth time he was slow
pauses.reason: Prepare the exact instant Garrick’s defense begins to fail.
Prepare the correction that turns apparent healing into temporary debt.
